prompt_inputs.content: Recent empirical studies demonstrate the intricate linkages between carbon pricing mechanisms and sectoral economic outcomes in developed economies. Climate scientists project that a 2°C warming threshold will trigger irreversible tipping points in Arctic permafrost systems, releasing methane deposits worth an estimated $43 trillion in stranded carbon assets. Simultaneously, environmental economists argue that carbon tax implementations reduce industrial competitiveness, with manufacturing sectors experiencing 3-8% productivity losses in the short term. Policy analysts contend that complementary green subsidies for renewable energy infrastructure can offset these losses while creating 2.3 million jobs annually, though distributional equity concerns persist regarding impacts on low-income communities dependent on fossil fuel industries.

solution_criteria: Extracts topics spanning at least three distinct domains (climate science, economics, and policy)
Separates interdisciplinary topics into distinct array elements rather than combining them
Returns output as a valid JSON array of strings
task_description: Extract topics out of a passage of text from a scholarly article into a JSON array of strings
scenario: Testing with a passage containing interdisciplinary topics spanning multiple domains (e.g., climate science, economics, and policy) to verify the prompt can identify and separate distinct subject areas

prompt_inputs.content: Machine learning approaches to natural language processing have revolutionized computational linguistics. Deep learning models, particularly neural networks and their specialized variants like recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer architectures, have become the dominant paradigm. Transformers, which rely on attention mechanisms, have proven especially effective for tasks such as machine translation, sentiment analysis, and named entity recognition. Within the broader context of artificial intelligence, natural language processing applications now power virtual assistants, chatbots, and information retrieval systems. Recent advances in large language models represent a convergence of transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, and massive-scale pretraining on diverse text corpora, enabling unprecedented performance on downstream language understanding tasks.

solution_criteria: Identifies all distinct topics at different levels of abstraction (e.g., machine learning, natural language processing, deep learning, neural networks, transformers, attention mechanisms, language models)
Appropriately handles hierarchical relationships where some topics are subtopics of others without unnecessary duplication or omission of parent or child topics
Returns results as a JSON array of strings with no additional metadata or structural hierarchy
task_description: Extract topics out of a passage of text from a scholarly article into a JSON array of strings
scenario: Testing with a passage containing overlapping or nested topics where some topics are subtopics of others to verify the prompt handles hierarchical relationships appropriately

prompt_inputs.content: The CRISPR-Cas9 system has revolutionized genome editing through its programmable DNA-targeting capabilities mediated by single-guide RNA (sgRNA) complexes. Recent advances in off-target mitigation employ high-fidelity Cas9 variants with enhanced PAM specificity and reduced mismatch tolerance, achieving >99% on-target selectivity. Concurrent developments in base editing, particularly cytosine-to-thymine (C-to-T) and adenine-to-guanine (A-to-G) conversions via fusion proteins containing deaminase domains, enable point mutations without double-strand breaks. Prime editing further extends the therapeutic potential by utilizing engineered reverse transcriptase-Cas9 fusion proteins to catalyze precise insertions, deletions, and transversions through a mechanism involving target-site priming and flap-equilibration dynamics.

solution_criteria: Extracts all major technical topics (CRISPR-Cas9, off-target mitigation, base editing, prime editing, etc.) from the specialized passage
Correctly identifies domain-specific terms and concepts as distinct topics
Returns topics as a valid JSON array of strings
Does not include extraneous words or incomplete topic names
task_description: Extract topics out of a passage of text from a scholarly article into a JSON array of strings
scenario: Testing with a dense, technical passage from a specialized field (e.g., quantum physics or biochemistry) containing domain-specific jargon to ensure proper topic extraction from highly specialized vocabulary

prompt_inputs.content: The interplay between cognitive load and information retention during asynchronous learning environments presents complex challenges for instructional design. When learners encounter fragmented content delivery across multiple platforms, their working memory becomes constrained, yet paradoxically, the spacing effect—the phenomenon where distributed practice enhances long-term encoding—suggests that such fragmentation, if strategically implemented, may facilitate deeper neural consolidation than massed presentation would achieve.

solution_criteria: Extracts both explicitly mentioned topics (cognitive load, information retention, asynchronous learning, instructional design, working memory, spacing effect) and inferred emergent themes (memory consolidation, learning design trade-offs)
Identifies implicit connections between concepts that are not stated directly but emerge from the passage context
Returns results as a JSON array of strings with no additional metadata
task_description: Extract topics out of a passage of text from a scholarly article into a JSON array of strings
scenario: Testing with a short, concise passage containing minimal explicit topic keywords but requiring inference from context to assess whether the prompt can extract implicit or emergent themes
